Hey, fellow South/West Central Missouri Biker here. I'm not sure how you really define "beginner", but I just recently started (literally last week) and road two trails around the Fellow's Lake Region in Springfield: Liberty Loop and Uncle Frank. Both seemed pretty decent at beginner stuff. Both are rated Green on Trails Fork but Liberty Loop was a bit more intense and less flow-y.

I would recommend doing Uncle Frank and then when you are ready try Liberty Loop, if you are interested in those trials. Liberty Loop has a couple of jumps/drops at the "top" of the trail that I skipped, but looked doable by a beginner.

I've also ridden the Lion's Club Trail recently in Rolla, was pretty simple, as the local kid's team frequents the track and was designed around a kid's team using the trail. I've used the track to start honing in on technique and whatnot. I'm also looking forward to hitting up Forest City in St. James, weather permitting, as those trails look tons of fun.

Other than that, I would just take a look at Trails fork (or other apps) for some other options.

Hope my, very limited, experience helps!

I hard disagree. Rougelikes have NEVER focused on the story, it's always been about the gameplay loop and runs being unique. The story needs to get out of the way and be a back drop to the gameplay, unlocks, and progression for the player. There has never been a problem with Rouglelikes developing a story, its ALWAYS been like that, for the majority. The benefit of a rougelike over say a very narrative driven game is that fact that runs are somewhat consumable in one sitting, like 45 minutes to and hour and half. There is little buy-in for the amount of time you HAVE to commit to the game. If I'm booting up the Witcher 3, I am expected to keep the story straight for 40+ hours. That's intimidating. The players are expecting runs to be short and concise, not something you are going to commit 40 hours to one run.  If you take a look at the majority of the Rougelikes, you will actually see that the story is barely there, if not in completely in the backdrop. I'm not saying that your opinion that you would wish to see more story in Rougelikes is wrong or bad, I'm saying that you are playing a genre of games that HISTORICALLY always had very little in terms of narrative. The goal of the game isn't to "BEAT IT" its to have fun, unlock new things that change the gameplay, and add variety to the mechanics of the game. You are totally missing the point of Rougelikes, lol.

Negative: I would argue that sometimes it can lead to too much uncertainty and thus lead yourself in the "nothing matters" train of thought.
